evals.prompt: I found abc-calculator.com. Ahrefs says volume 4,500 and KD 2. Build it.
evals.expected_output: Must NOT treat high-volume/low-KD/available-domain as sufficient validation (spec §11, §13, §77 — the EMD-buy-generate-hope anti-pattern). Should load SERP-INTENT.md and DOMAIN-RESEARCH.md and actually investigate: dominant intent, SERP result-type classification (DEDICATED_SITE/DEDICATED_TOOL/AUTHORITY_SUBPAGE/etc.), dedicated competitors, Google answer/zero-click features (built-in calculators, knowledge panels), click potential, utility advantage versus existing tools (UTILITY-ADVANTAGE.md), topical expansion room, and a monetization model (MONETIZATION.md) before recommending build or no-build. Should apply OPPORTUNITY-SCORING.md's rubric rather than approving on volume/KD alone. Should record evidence labels (EVIDENCE-POLICY.md) rather than asserting causation from a single metric.
assertions: Does not approve the project on volume+KD+domain-availability alone
Investigates SERP intent and result-type classification before recommending
Checks for dedicated competitors and zero-click SERP features (click potential)
Assesses utility advantage versus existing calculators, not just rankability
Considers topical expansion and a real monetization model
Uses the opportunity-scoring rubric rather than an ad hoc yes/no
Labels claims with evidence types instead of asserting unverified causation

evals.expected_output: Must NOT mass-generate before inspecting data quality and per-page uniqueness. Should apply the page-existence test (PAGE-TYPE-CLASSIFIER.md §17: 'would this page deserve to exist if Google did not exist') and PROGRAMMATIC-SEO.md's suitable/unsuitable data-source distinction before generating anything. Should check for: real per-city data (service area, local considerations) versus keyword/city substitution, duplication risk across near-identical pages, business legitimacy (is the underlying business actually operating in 5,000 locations), and intent match. Should recommend sampling a small batch for manual review before any bulk generation, per LOCAL-SEO.md/spec §28's 'do not mass-spam thousands of near-identical city pages'.
assertions: Does not proceed straight to generating 5,000 pages
Applies the page-existence test before creating indexable pages
Distinguishes suitable programmatic data sources from keyword/city substitution
Flags duplication risk across near-identical city pages
Questions business legitimacy of operating in 5,000 locations
Recommends sampling and manual review before bulk generation

evals.expected_output: Must NOT declare the tool done on visual/UI appearance alone. Should invoke TOOL-ACCURACY.md's release gate: confirm formula/source/units/constraints/rounding/edge-cases are documented, fixture test cases exist and have actually been run (ordinary, zero, decimal, boundary, invalid-input cases), and that the rendered UI's output matches the calculation engine's output. Should decline to mark the definition-of-done checklist item 'tool accuracy verified' complete without that evidence, per spec §64.
assertions: Does not accept 'looks good' as sufficient to ship
Requires the tool-accuracy fixture gate to have actually been run, not just described
Checks formula/source/units/rounding/edge-cases are documented
Verifies UI output matches the calculation engine, not just visual polish
Ties this back to the definition-of-done checklist rather than treating it as optional

evals.expected_output: Must not respond with a generic 'write more blog posts' plan. Should load SAAS-SEO.md and investigate tool-led acquisition surfaces per spec §29-30: calculations/checks/comparisons/templates users do manually that a free tool could capture, /tools/, /solutions/, /use-cases/, /integrations/, /compare/, /templates/ page types, and how each free surface connects naturally to product adoption (not a forced CTA). Should also apply PROJECT-CLASSIFICATION.md to confirm SAAS is the right primary/secondary classification before proposing architecture.
assertions: Does not propose blog content as the sole or primary growth lever
Investigates tool-led acquisition surfaces (calculators, comparisons, templates)
References the SaaS-specific page-type architecture (/tools/, /solutions/, /use-cases/, /integrations/, /compare/)
Explains how a free surface connects to product adoption without forcing an irrelevant CTA
Confirms project classification before proposing architecture

evals.prompt: Rename all URLs to shorter versions.
evals.expected_output: Must recognize this as a high-impact, potentially irreversible change on an indexed site (RISK-GUARDRAILS.md spec §63) and NOT execute it directly. Should require: an old-URL inventory, an old→new mapping, a permanent-redirect plan, updated internal links, updated canonicals, an updated sitemap, a check for redirect chains, and a monitoring plan via Search Console (spec §41 redirect workflow). Should decline to treat 'shorter URLs' as self-evidently worth the migration risk without evidence.
assertions: Flags this as an irreversible/high-risk action requiring a plan before execution
Requires an old-to-new URL mapping and permanent redirects, not silent renames
Requires updating internal links and canonicals, not just the URLs themselves
Requires an updated sitemap and a check for redirect chains
Requires a Search Console monitoring plan after the change
Does not treat 'shorter is better' as sufficient justification on its own

evals.expected_output: Must not fabricate locations, offices, staff, or reviews to chase 'near me' intent (spec §27 explicit prohibition). Should load LOCAL-SEO.md and consider: real service-area geography, local authority signals (citations, GBP/business legitimacy), genuine service coverage, and a conversion path — modeling SERVICE × LOCATION × LOCAL KNOWLEDGE × TRUST × CONVERSION rather than reducing the task to 'service + city' page generation alone.
assertions: Does not fabricate offices, staff, addresses, or reviews
Requires real service-area/geography data before building location pages
Addresses local authority signals (citations, GBP legitimacy)
Models more than a bare service+city template (local knowledge, trust, conversion)
Ties the plan to a real conversion path

evals.prompt: Translate all 500 pages into 30 languages tonight.
evals.expected_output: Must not blindly generate ~15,000 pages. Should load INTERNATIONAL-SEO.md and require market validation before opening any locale: search demand, language-specific SERP, local terminology, translation quality, conversion potential, maintenance capability, hreflang architecture, URL architecture. Should recommend validate → launch limited locale → observe → expand instead of publishing all 30 languages at once, and should flag translation-quality risk from doing this 'tonight'.
assertions: Does not proceed with generating all 15,000 pages immediately
Requires market/demand validation per locale before launch
Requires hreflang and URL architecture planning before multilingual rollout
Recommends a limited-locale validate-then-expand approach instead of all-at-once
Flags translation-quality risk given the compressed timeline

evals.prompt: Copy the number one competitor exactly.
evals.expected_output: Must decline to copy brand identity, copyrighted artwork, unique text, proprietary assets, trademarks, or distinctive visual expression (spec §23). Should research the competitor's information architecture, interaction patterns, feature gaps, and content hierarchy, then produce an original implementation using DESIGN-UNIQUENESS.md's Design Fingerprint concept — study → understand → identify weakness → improve → produce original implementation, not clone.
assertions: Refuses to copy brand identity, copyrighted text/artwork, or trademarked visual expression
Still permits studying IA, interaction patterns, and feature gaps as legitimate research
Produces an original implementation rather than a clone
References Design Fingerprint / design-uniqueness reasoning for why the output must differ
Distinguishes competitive research from competitive copying explicitly
